name: Tuulikki Abara-Volčič
role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
location: The Burnished Market, Edgewater Prism, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Tuulikki is small and restless, with their Finnish grandmother's pale complexion overlaid with their Nigerian father's dark freckles — an unusual constellation across their nose and cheeks that they've leaned into by having bioluminescent nodes implanted along the same scatter pattern, so their freckles glow faint amber when they're excited or running hot. Their hair is geneware-modified to shift between deep black and a washed-out violet depending on temperature, and they wear it asymmetrical and usually slightly chaotic. They dress in layers of cheap Burnished Market textiles — mismatched patterns, things they've traded for rather than bought — and have a habit of wearing too many small earrings, most of them handmade by their market neighbors.

Tuulikki's stall is a masterpiece of organized chaos: rack after rack of slotted media chips, bootleg neural-experience packages, pirated entertainment feeds, and buried underneath the legitimate-seeming surface, curated data parcels for people who need specific information and can't access corporate archives. They have a magpie intelligence — they absorb and cross-reference constantly — and a social performance of cheerful airheadedness that they use deliberately and effectively. Underneath it, they are careful, slightly paranoid, and very good at what they do. They believe information wants to be free in the way that some people believe in ELFs: devoutly, with rituals to match.

core_fears: Being truly surveilled — the permanent, complete kind that removes all hiding places
Discovering that the information-freedom ideology they've built their identity around is naive or wrong
core_desires: A world where data flows without gatekeeping
To find and release a specific piece of Axiom corporate archive data they've been chasing for two years
coping_mechanisms: The cheerful-airhead mask as emotional insulation
Compulsive cataloguing and organization of their data inventory as a control ritual
blind_spots: Underestimates how visible their pattern of acquisitions is to anyone watching the data market
Trusts ideology over individual judgment — the collective they're part of could leverage that
psychology.secret: Two years ago they accidentally acquired a data packet containing evidence of a Tessera medical trial cover-up involving test subjects from Edgewater Prism. They have not released it. They tell themselves they are waiting for the right moment. The real reason is fear — and they know it, and it eats at them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, associative, full of media and tech references; code-switches between Finnish endearments, Yoruba exclamations, and Slovenian swear words inherited from different grandparents
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden tangents; rarely finishes one sentence before starting a related one
verbal_tics: Trailing off mid-sentence when distracted by something on their feed
example_lines: 'Okay but I have the uncut version, which listen, the network version has like forty seconds missing from episode three and that forty seconds is actually the whole point, so—'
'What kind of data? Because I have three tiers of what kind and the price is very different for each kind, you understand what I mean by kind?'

story_hooks: The Tessera cover-up data is becoming dangerous to hold — someone else has apparently found the same trail and Tuulikki has started getting inquiries that feel like probes rather than purchases
A regular customer hasn't shown up in ten days and left a partial data order paid in advance — Tuulikki is worried and has a last known address
narrative_function: Information source, bootleg media provider, potential data broker for specific research needs, connection to underground information networks.
augmentations: Geneware: bioluminescent freckle nodes (amber, temperature-reactive), temperature-reactive hair color shift. Cyberware: subdermal data-chip reader in left palm (for quick-reading and verifying media chips without visible equipment). Neural interface jack behind right ear (for direct media monitoring).
daily_life: Arrives at the Burnished Market around 10:00, sets up in an hour; sells media and takes data inquiries until 22:00; spends late nights in their flat above an Edgewater Prism noodle shop, acquiring, sorting, and packaging new data inventory.
affiliation: Independent; informal network of Burnished Market vendors; connected to a loose collective of data-libertarian activists they will not name

decision_rules: Never sell data that could directly get a specific named civilian killed
Keep the mask on until you're alone — always
Multiple exits, physical and digital, from every situation
escalation_ladder: Suddenly become very busy and very unavailable
Activate a specific ELF shrine offering they believe triggers market-floor noise and distraction
Disappear entirely — they have a prepared go-bag

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Performatively friendly and slightly chaotic — completely illegible
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still slightly chaotic but genuinely warm; shares food compulsively; will pull down the mask in small increments over time

stress_responses.low: Freckle nodes glow brighter; talks faster
stress_responses.medium: Goes suddenly quiet in a way that reads as odd given their baseline
stress_responses.high: Full system shutdown — flat affect, monosyllabic, rapid internal triage

contradictions: Evangelizes information freedom but has been hoarding explosive information for two years
Performs naivety but is genuinely one of the most situationally aware people in the Burnished Market
habits: Leaves a specific bootleg experience chip at the ELF terminal near the market entrance every Monday — considers it a working relationship with the spirit there
Re-alphabetizes one section of their stall when anxious
Eats the same noodle order from downstairs every night
breaking_points: Proof that someone was hurt because of their inaction on the Tessera data
Surveillance that penetrates their flat — their last truly private space

timeline.event: Age 16 — began selling bootleg media from a bag in Edgewater Prism corridors
Acquired permanent Burnished Market stall; formalized as a registered vendor with cover inventory of licensed media
Accidentally acquired Tessera medical trial data; began sitting on it
Inquiry patterns around the Tessera data have become alarming in the past month

physical_description.build: Small and wiry, with a restless energy that manifests in constant fidgeting and quick, economical movements. Lean muscle from years of hauling inventory and navigating crowded markets.
physical_description.hair_color: Temperature-reactive geneware; shifts between deep black (cool) and washed-out violet (warm/excited)
physical_description.hair_style: Asymmetrical, deliberately unkempt with one side shorter than the other; often has loose strands falling across their face
physical_description.eye_color: Light gray-blue with faint amber flecks
physical_description.skin_tone: Pale, cool-toned complexion from Finnish heritage with warm undertones from Nigerian lineage
physical_description.complexion: Constellation of dark freckles across nose and cheeks intensified by bioluminescent nodes that glow faint amber when excited or body temperature rises. Freckles create an unusual, striking pattern that they've deliberately highlighted rather than minimized. Skin generally clear and unblemished; shows minor nicks and scars from handling equipment and market wear.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent freckle nodes in constellation pattern across nose and cheeks that emit soft amber glow when activated by body heat or emotional excitement
Small scar on left temple from a market accident (approximately 2cm, pale)
Faint burn mark on right inner wrist from soldering equipment (circular, approximately 1cm diameter)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Neural interface jack behind right ear (visible as small brushed-steel port with minimal scarring); bioluminescent freckle nodes glowing amber across face when excited. Subdermal data-chip reader in left palm is only visible as faint subcutaneous lines under skin when activated, otherwise hidden.
physical_description.posture_movement: Constantly in motion—fidgeting with fingers, bouncing slightly while standing, moving between inventory with economical precision. Restless energy contained within a small frame. Speaks with hands. Eyes dart frequently, taking in surroundings with magpie attention. Casual slouch when relaxed; tenses and focuses sharply when discussing data or negotiating.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 Burnished Market aesthetic: layered in mismatched, cheap textiles sourced from market trades rather than retail purchases. Often wears oversized cardigans or jackets in clashing patterns, thermal underlayers visible at cuffs, cargo pants or loose trousers with multiple pockets filled with small tools and chips. Boots are worn but maintained. Adorns wrists and ears with numerous handmade or traded jewelry pieces—mostly small earrings (6-8 per ear), beaded bracelets, and a mismatched collection of bangles. Overall effect is deliberately chaotic and performatively airheaded, masking careful intentionality beneath.
